references.text: The man who was possessed by demons met Jesus and fell down before him – this is the context for his desire to go with Jesus after being freed.
The man whom the demons had left was found sitting at Jesus' feet, clothed and in his right mind – this shows his transformation and attachment to Jesus as the background for his wish to follow him.
Jesus sends the man away with instructions to tell what God has done for him, instead of letting him come along – this is the direct continuation and Jesus' alternative to the man's request.
The parallel account in Mark, where the man who had been possessed asks to be allowed to go with Jesus, but Jesus sends him home to tell what the Lord has done.
In Mark's version, the man goes and proclaims in Decapolis what Jesus has done for him, showing the result of Jesus sending him away.
The man born blind who was healed believed in Jesus and worshiped him – a similar example of someone who has been freed and wishes to be near Jesus.
The Samaritan leper who was cleansed and returned to thank Jesus – a similar example of gratitude and the desire to stay with Jesus after being healed.
People who wanted to follow Jesus but were given other instructions – a parallel theme that following Jesus can take different forms.
Matthew's parallel account about the possessed men and the demons entering the pigs, although Matthew does not mention the man's wish to follow Jesus.
